claims.claim_text: The qualified source checkpoint used single-step signal/risk meta-training but no event-label joint representation training; source test performance alone is not adaptation evidence.

The present HDF5 partitions contain processed flat23 features; TRAIN has 401 event intervals in 327 shots, including 158 safe event-bearing shots, and median recorded spans differ substantially between source training and target test.
Event annotations are offline model-generated weak labels with upstream split exposure; state recognition is not a validated disruption mechanism or proof of adaptable representations.
Cross-device literature motivates semantic alignment and trajectory-sensitive prediction but often uses target data or label access unavailable in the requested zero-label start.
Source preparation for adaptation, auxiliary-task usefulness, and delayed observation access require explicit evaluation; reconstruction improvement alone is insufficient.

An event-assisted causal model whose single risk head reads predicted short-term evolution, with source-trained sequential adaptation, is a testable next hypothesis, not an established result or novelty claim.
The last two decoder-scope runs completed but failed the target criterion and are archived, not promoted.

manifest_negative_constraints.rule: No claim of independent test confirmation, new physical law, or 100 fully read papers.
Do not count signal reconstruction gains, alarm tuning, retrospective threshold selection or inter-shot gains as pure intra-shot success.
Keep J-TEXT TEST220 lead>10ms and EAST TEST360 lead>30ms; no target labels or whole-stream statistics before the first EAST shot.
Do not infer physical units or exact diagnostic definitions solely from feature names; no deliberate weakening of the naked-transfer baseline.
